text:
cheng: Heads-up — ran a trunk perf sweep this morning and saw a weird 95/99p latency spike for small-batch decode on the new fused-paged FlashAttention variant. Idle prefill looks fine, but decode microbursts go from ~12ms to ~45ms occasionally. :thinking:
kate: ugh. is this the change that switched kernel routing to favor fusion+paged by default?
cheng: yeah, the kernel toggle landed in #4821 last week. My suspicion: continuous-batching scheduler is routing decode microbatches into the paged-fused kernel that expects larger steady-state KV locality. When the KV cache misses (cold or fragmented hotset) the kernel stalls and occupancy drops.
leo: can you paste the perf numbers and a quick flame/trace? even a couple samples help.
cheng: quick paste from the profiler (-a = agg over 3000 requests):
```
--decode-smallbatch--
kernel: fused_paged_flash_v2
p50: 11.8ms p90: 14.3ms p95: 20.9ms p99: 44.7ms
kv-miss-rate (decode windows): 18% -> tail spikes
gpu-active %: 67% (on spike samples drops to 22%)
SM occupancy: 78% -> 19% on spike
```
leo: that occupancy collapse matches a thread divergence / sync stall pattern. do we see large memcpy spikes or cross-block reductions?
cheng: nvprof slice shows a ~2.1ms memcpy peak right before decode kernel on the bad traces; on good traces memcpy ~= 80us. Looks like extra KV page faults followed by CPU-driven page fetchs into pinned buffer.
olivia: wow. are these requests hitting paged attention because of sequence lengths or because of the kernel routing heuristic?
cheng: routing is mostly based on (seq_len, batch_size, kvpage_enabled) right now. decode microbatches are small batch_size but sometimes long seq_len due to conversation history forwarded from prefill. scheduler didn't account for sudden KV sparsity on decode vs prefill.
kate: what's the quick mitigation? revert the toggle or tweak routing?
cheng: short-term: pin decode path to the small-batch decode kernel when (batch_size <= 4 && latency_slo <= 50ms) — that avoids paged-fused kernel. Longer term: add a microburst detector in the continuous-batching loop that watches recent kv-miss-rate and forces decode-routing to low-occupancy-robust kernels.
leo: ok. wanna try a bench run with pinned decode kernel + perf-flag? I can spin CI. Which config?
cheng: use this runtime override in the bench harness:
```
runtime.routing.override = {
  "prefer_fused_for": "prefill",
  "prefer_small_for": "decode",
  "small_batch_threshold": 4
}
```
bench link: https://ci.internal/bench/2026/rt-7593 (short run, 5k reqs)
perf-bot: bench rt-7593 finished: p99 decode latency 13.1ms (baseline 44.7ms), cost +0.4%, throughput unchanged. artifacts: /artifacts/rt-7593/trace.tar.gz
olivia: that's promising. any quality regressions from using the small-batch kernel for decode?
cheng: no model output diffs in the test harness (deterministic model variant). decoding throughput slightly lower for large sustained batches, but decode microburst latency is now stable.
kate: can we make the heuristic adaptive rather than a hard pin? i.e., prefer small kernel when recent kv-miss-rate > X or when scheduler sees backpressure?
leo: yes — propose a simple EWMA over kv-miss-rate across the last N decode windows. if EWMA > 10% then route decode to small kernel. cheap to implement and should be safe.
cheng: I'll draft the change as a small patch: (1) add kv-miss EWMA to scheduler state, (2) routing rule: if decoder and EWMA > 0.10 -> force small-kernel, (3) expose runtime flag to override.
olivia: please open a PR and include the bench artifact and a brief explanation in the changelog. assign to leo for review.
cheng: opened PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rt/compare/pr-4987 — includes tests + bench artifacts. cc @leo
leo: reviewing today. if all green we can roll the heuristic behind a feature flag and enable on canary nodes tomorrow. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: rollout candidate created: canary=5 nodes, flag=decode-kv-ewma-route, smoke-tests pending.
cheng: thanks all — follow-up: i'll add a small-unit test simulating fragmented KV hotset and document the config in runtime docs.
kate: nice find, thanks for the quick mitigation. :clap:
